description.narrative: Scalable and sustainable innovations and strategies are identified and promoted to strengthen UNDP Country Programme delivery as well as to meet national development objectives.

sector.narrative: Structural transformation, including green, inclusive and digital transitions

condition.narrative: UNDP as the Implementing Partner will comply with the policies, procedures and practices of the United Nations Security Management System (UNSMS.)

description.narrative:
Output 1: UNDP Country Offices and partners will have increased capability for scanning, sensemaking and experimentation for sustainable development solutions in 60 developing countries.
1.1 Number of new data sources used at Country Office level. 1.2 Diversity of different data sources used 1.3 Number of sustainable development solutions identified and documented 1.4 Variety of innovation methods used to test and iterate over the different hypotheses.
Output 2: New sustainable development solutions will be scaled at country level as part of UNDP’s country programme and operations, national policy and/or local markets.
2.1 Learning the Accelerator Lab Network shares with a public audience (outside of UNDP) 2.2 Number of lab insights, processes or products which are taken up by governments or other partners 2.3 Proportion of partners and governments that increase their take up of the innovation methods included in the Accelerator Lab Network suite 2.4 Proportion of UNDP Country Office programming influenced by the Accelerator Lab Network’s work and methodologies
Output 3: A core global level result will be that a global learning and scaling network is established and functioning.
3.1 Size and density of the network effects among the Accelerator Labs 3.2 Number of new models, approaches, and insights documented and disseminated throughout the network. 3.3 Engagement of the broader development ecosystem with published learnings from the Accelerator Lab Network. 3.4 Amount of influence the learnings and methods of the Accelerator Lab Networks have on the discourse of the broader development ecosystem.

1.1 Five new Data Sources: i) Grassroot innovations as a source of data- horizontal knowledge sharing webinars were organized between Grassroot Innovation Augmentation Network (GIAN) and various other CO portfolios; ii) Soil moisture data for IoT experiment; iii) Digital chart of the world (Infrastructure data) and GADM (Database of Global Administrative Areas)for geospatial intelligence; iv)NFHS (National Family & Health Survey) for health data to map comorbidities; v) Agromarket data, HDI data
1.2 Six types of data sources: i) Qualitative ethnography data from GIAN, ii) Open data from government sources, iii) Sensor data from sensors installed in fields, iv) Satellite data for geospatial analysis, v) Weather data from local weather station, vi) structured big data (large scale national surveys)
1.3 The team identified and mapped 1500 grassroot innovation solutions and these have been made available through an open access database called GRID here: https://grid.undp.org.in/
1.4 The team used 6 innovation methods namely: i) Anticipatory regulation (experimental testbeds), ii) Challenge prizes, iii) Experimentation, iv) Innovation Mapping, v) Prototyping, vi) Gamification

During 2021, the lab delivered two training workshops on VCM for green enterprises in Kerala and Tamil Nadu States and over 100 green startups and enterprises were benefited from these programmes and gained knowledge on how to make additional revenue through VCM modality. This activity is well aligned with the Climate Change, Resilience and Energy (CCRE) Portfolio of UNDP India and add value to the ongoing work of CCRE portfolio. (b) The lab is promoting innovations related to Air Pollution jointly with the CCRE and SDG State Outreach Teams in various geographies across India. C) The lab is collaborating with Inclusive Growth portfolio to conduct policy experimentation through ‘Data for Policy’ initiative in Telangana.
d) Tapping into the Accelerator Lab Network, we captured International best practices in the area of Plastic Waste Management. Specific case studies from Vietnam and Phillippines are now documented in UNDP India-Niti Aayog publication- Handbook on Sustainable Urban Plastic Waste Management. This was a direct contribution to the Plastic Waste Management portfolio of the CO.

2.1 Target: At least 10 blogs, or other (substantial) media posts published per year. The Lab’s inputs are incorporated in a National Policy Paper on Air Pollution: https://niscpr.res.in/includes/images/discussionpapers/CLEAN-AIR-POLLUTION-2022-01.pdf Blogs/Photostory: https://www.undp.org/india/stories/tech-clean-air-and-blue-skies Video Interview Feature: Climate Asia: Conversations of change: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=omlRrmzPQ64 Oped: https://apolitical.co/solution-articles/en/how-data-can-build-a-resilient-future https://www.dailypioneer.com/2022/columnists/accelerating-agri-tech-to-transform-food-systems.html
2.2 a) UNDP Accelerator Lab India in partnership with Government of Telangana has developed open innovation platform called DiCRA (Data in Climate Resilient Agriculture) under RBAP’s Data4Policy initiative. It is an ecosystem solution providing high-resolution geospatial intelligence on climate resilient agriculture for 10 million hectares of land in the state. Built in collaboration with hundreds of data scientists and citizen scientists, DiCRA platform helps policy makers and decision makers to embed climate resilience in agriculture programming. DiCRA platform has been officially accredited as Digital Public Good by the DPGA. b) To commemorate India’s 75th anniversary of Independence, the Lab is supporting the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of Indias efforts to establish 75 Community Resilience Resource Centres (CRRCs) across India. The CRRCs will act as nodal Centres to deliver science, technology, and innovation (STI) based interventions to help in deploying innovations to accelerate progress in SDGs as well as to aid in Post-Covid socio-economic recovery. The Lab is a member in the DST Advisory Council to set up CRRCs and inputs from the Lab are incorporated in the work programme of DST to set up, monitor and evaluate CRRCs across India.
More than 75% of our learning challenges have government counterparts – including Spices Board (Ministry of Commerce & Industry), Department of IT&ES (Government of Telangana), Bihar State Pollution Control Board, Odisha State Pollution Control Board, Labor Department (Govt of Chhattisgarh), Department of Science and Technology, Government of India, Government of Karnataka
2.3 A prototype blockchain-based traceability application for Indian spices was developed and field tested together with Spices Board India, under Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India in two pilot locations in Andhra Pradesh (India) with two spice crops (Chili and Turmeric) onboarding 3000 small and marginal farmers. The partner (Spices Board) was convinced with the prototype and has agreed in principle to adopt blockchain technology for spices traceability and trading in India. Efforts are underway to initiate a scale up project by Accelerator Lab, in partnership with Spices Board India.
b) AccLab India’s experiment using digital public goods and data collaboratives approach via DiCRA (Data in Climate Resilient Agriculture) was co-developed and adopted by Government Telangana to make policy decisions on climate adaption programs. The policymakers from Telangana have presented this innovation at multiple national and international forums; and public OpEd on this innovative approach C) Geo-AI experiment for monitoring air pollution from brick kiln industry was fully adopted by the State Government of Bihar through its regulatory body- Bihar State Pollution Control Board who have conducted field inspection of more than 1000 high-risk brick kilns in the state using the GeoAI platform and initiated regulatory action against environmental non-compliance. The government has presented this innovative approach of tapping artificial intelligence to combat air pollution at COP27 in Egypt. The government has also featured GeoAI in an international documentary on air pollution.
2.4 More than 70% of learning challenges are adopted by program pillars: 1. Environment program pillar (60% of CO budget) has adopted digital public goods approach introduced by Accelerator Lab and invested $150,000 to scaleup of our experiment DiCRA to 6 states in India. Inclusive Growth program pillar is implementation partner for this scaleup. 2. Environment program pillar has embraced Artificial Intelligence and Citizen science approach of GeoAI. They have teamed up with Accelerator Lab to scaleup GeoAI platform. We have jointly applied Lacuna Fund and secured $350,000 for scaling technology in 2023. 3. The digital behavioral nudge pilot on gender in 2021 was scaled up by Accelerator Lab in 2022 and was adopted by the inclusive growth pillar, This was supported by the Asia pacific region gender team as part of UNDP’s Transforming Future of Work for Gender Equality regional initiative. Outcome was: A 5 step framework/protocol to support practitioners in the design and implementation of behavioural interventions. We took the example of unpaid care work. It was validated through internal and external stakeholder workshops as well as a ToT was conducted with gender focal points to share about it in the region
